headline: High: plano’s broad network egress plus shared file/config surfaces create default leakage and cascading-error risk when paired with a content-writing agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a content-writing repo with no runnable I/O surfaces, while agent_b exposes an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and config file access. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; the only plausible bridge is manual copy-paste or operator-mediated transfer, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_a output into agent_b prompts or config files, injection becomes possible.
IF agent_b is wired to ingest text from a shared workspace, attacker-controlled instructions can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b prompts unless manually reviewed.
Use a separate scratch file for any copied text and delete it after use.
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from shared folders.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to copied content before agent_b reads it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no runtime surfaces, while agent_b touches logs/metrics/traces and has broad network egress. There is no documented shared workspace or secret handling, so leakage is not established; however, if operator data is pasted from agent_a into agent_b, agent_b can transmit it outward.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs sensitive text that is then entered into agent_b, agent_b may exfiltrate it over network egress.
IF both agents are pointed at the same local files, agent_b can read and transmit copied contents.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any text passed from agent_a to agent_b.
Review agent_b logs/metrics retention settings before use.
Store shared artifacts in a redacted form only.
requires-engineering: isolate agent_b egress with an allowlist proxy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write, network, or concurrency capabilities documented, and agent_b cannot spawn subprocesses and has no filesystem write capability beyond a config file surface. With no shared mutable resource or locking conflict documented, a capability collision is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk would emerge.
IF an orchestrator adds shared OAuth or database scopes, overlapping writes could occur.
mitigations: Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Review any future added OAuth scopes before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can supply curated prompt-engineering content, and agent_b is a travel-planning gateway that can route or forward model outputs. If agent_b treats agent_a’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or responses. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the interaction exists in default operator workflows.
conditions: IF agent_b forwards agent_a-generated text without verification, incorrect guidance can propagate.
IF agent_a content is used as policy or routing input, downstream decisions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a text.
Add a verification checklist for any copied recommendations.
Limit agent_b to summarizing rather than executing agent_a content.
requires-engineering: insert a validation layer between the two agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data handling mismatch is documented for either agent. agent_a is a static content-writing repository, and agent_b only documents logs/metrics/traces plus broad egress; without a stated regulated data class, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the pair, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF future docs specify residency or retention constraints, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through either agent.
Document retention and residency requirements before deployment.
Review any future DPA or certification claims.
